intro: A Los Angeles garage-punk band, led by Laena Myers.
story: FEELS is the Los Angeles band fronted by Laena Geronimo, with Shannon Lay, Amy Allen and the drummer Michael Perry Rudes; Rudes and Lay had played in her solo project Raw Geronimo before it became FEELS in 2016. Their self-titled debut was recorded with Ty Segall in one day-long session, and Post Earth came out on Wichita on February 22, 2019, produced by Tim Green; DIY called it a terrific out-and-out rock record. They played Pickathon in 2022, a year after Subversive Reaction. Myers has since worked on solo music and string sessions for other records.

intro: A Lafayette band keeping Cajun music alive since 1999.
story: Feufollet came together in Lafayette, Louisiana, in the late 1990s, when the members were kids who learned French Cajun repertoire in French immersion school. En Couleurs was nominated for the Grammy for Best Zydeco or Cajun Music Album and won Best Cajun Band at New Orleans's Big Easy Music Awards. Two Universes came out on March 24, 2015, their first album in five years, with Kelli Jones-Savoy replacing Anna Laura Edmiston, and NPR's World Cafe said it is a pop album and a very good one. They played Pickathon in 2022. Prends Courage, a retrospective of unreleased recordings, came out in 2019, and in 2026 current and former members gathered for a retrospective set at the Louisiana Cajun-Zydeco Fest.

intro: A Nashville songwriter of plain, moving Americana.
story: Gabe Lee is a Nashville native and the son of Taiwanese immigrants, one of few Asian-American songwriters in Nashville's Americana scene. Farmland was his 2019 debut, and Honky Tonk Hell came on March 13, 2020, its title track co-written with Marcus King; Saving Country Music said he will be one of the next great artists in country and roots. The Hometown Kid, recorded at Nashville's Farmland Studio, came out in 2022, the year he played Pickathon, and Drink the River on Torrez in 2023. In 2026 he worked the Southeast and the Pacific Northwest.
artist_reel_line: The Hometown Kid came out in 2022, recorded at Nashville's Farmland Studio.

intro: Griff Washburn, who writes songs aboard a sailboat.
story: Goth Babe is the solo project of Griff Washburn, begun in 2015 in Tennessee; the name comes from a Surf Curse song. He moved to the West Coast in 2017 and lived and toured in a van. His 2018 single "Sometimes" passed 9 million Spotify streams by September 2019, the year of the Mt. Hood EP. He played Pickathon in 2022. His debut album, Lola, came out on Mom + Pop in 2024, and he lives on an off-grid sailboat of the same name.
artist_reel_line: Lola, his debut album, came out on Mom + Pop in 2024.

intro: A London post-punk band on Sub Pop.
story: TV Priest is a London post-punk quartet formed in 2019, Charlie Drinkwater, Alex Sprogis, Nic Bueth and Ed Kelland, who signed to Sub Pop after playing a single gig, in an industrial freezer in November 2019. Uppers came out on February 5, 2021, and The Line of Best Fit said it should rubber-stamp them as one of the best new acts. My Other People followed on June 17, 2022, the summer they played Pickathon. A new album, Cartoons, is due on November 27, 2026.
